messages:
laura: Heads-up: after the kernel-selector tweak last night we're seeing a P99 regression (~2-3x) on qwen2.5 for short multilingual prompts. repro is pretty consistent on prod-dedicated pool. :eyes:
kevin: ugh. is this across all seq lengths or only short ones?
jia: short (<64) and mixed-language (zh + en) seems worst. Long sequences look fine.
sam: any sign of KV-cache misses or extra memcpy in the profiler?
maria: I ran a quick nvprof / nvtx trace on a repro instance. hotspots pointed to a tiny kernel launching a fallback attention path a lot. My guess: kernel selector picks an ALiBi/rope variant that mismatches cached KV layout -> forces remap.
perf-bot: perf summary: baseline commit 1769999000 -> 184k tokens/s; after selector change -> 62k tokens/s for short multilingual batch of 1. memcpy and kernel-launch overhead increased.
laura: exact repro command I used: ```
./tools/bench_local --model qwen2.5 --prompt-file repro/multilang_short.txt --max-tokens 64 --batch-size 1 --iters 500 --trace nvtx --profile
```
kevin: can you paste the nvprof stack? even a top-10 is fine.
maria: top kernels (by time):
- attention_fused_alibi_kernel (32.4%)
- kv_cache_repack_kernel (21.1%)
- softmax_stable_kernel (9.0%)
- memcpy H2D/D2H (14.2% combined)
- kernel launch overhead (async)

maria: note: attention_fused_alibi_kernel is the new path the selector prefers for qwen2.5 when detect_multilang_tokenizer==true and rope_scale!=1.0
jia: that matches my local trace. Also tokenizer emits mixed token lengths for zh+en and our batcher affinity groups don't coalesce, so we often send tiny batches with different seq-lengths across warps which trips a fallback kernel.
sam: so two interacting issues: (1) kernel selection chooses ALiBi-fused kernel that expects a specific kv layout/stride, (2) batching heuristic creates non-uniform micro-batches so remap happens per request.
kevin: quick experiment ideas:
- force kernel selector to prefer the legacy causal kernel for qwen2.5 on short sequences (env override)
- try rope_scale=1.0 vs rope_scale=0.75 and see if mapping path differs
- change batcher: group by (lang_family, seq_bucket) before sending to runtime

laura: I tried forcing legacy kernel with --kernels=legacy and perf went back to ~170k tokens/s for the same workload (still slightly below baseline).
maria: interesting. That suggests remap cost is dominant, not algorithmic difference.
perf-bot: quick diff of selector heuristics: new_selector chooses alibi_fused when: model==qwen2.5 && seq<=64 && tokenizer_multilang==true && rope_scale!=1.0
kevin: maybe the original intent was to use ALiBi for multilingual prompt handling, but the fused kernel assumes kv_head_dim aligned to 64 multiples. Qwen2.5 has kv_head_dim=80 for some variants -> misaligned strides.
laura: yes, the mismatch was subtle: kv_head_dim != attention_head_dim in a few model configs. We didn't assert alignment in selector.
jia: short-term patch: add a guard in selector: require kv_head_dim % 64 == 0 for fused_alibi kernel. Should remove regression quickly.
sam: mid-term: add a remap-less execution path in fused kernel for non-64-aligned kv dims (vectorized fallback), avoids expensive repack.
maria: also update batching: prefer aggregation by tokenizer fingerprint (language detection hash) to reduce mixed-language microbatches that flip selector heuristics per request.
kevin: testing checklist:
1) rollout selector guard to canary group (10% traffic)
2) run bench harness with repro suite (multilang_short + various seq buckets)
3) capture nvtx traces and compare memcpy & kernel-launch counts
4) if stable, expand rollouts and merge kernel improvement PR

laura: I'll open the canary PR. attaching the minimal repro prompt and perf traces in the PR.
maria: tagged @eng-oncall in the PR for watch during canary.
infra-bot: deploy triggered: canary selector-guard -> prod-dedicated pool (10%): deploy_id=deploy-2026-11-09-17:04
kevin: follow-up experiments to log: rope_scale interplay (0.75/1.0/1.25), ALiBi vs RoPE variants, tokenizer normalization toggle (byte-level vs unicode-normalized), batcher grouping by language-id.
laura: one more oddity: when we force rope_scale=1.0 performance improves but output quality vs baseline drops on some instruction-following prompts. so can't blindly change rope_scale; need per-model/per-task config.
jia: agreed. add model-variant feature flag so customers pinned to a version don't get behavior change.
sam: ok next actions: laura PR for selector guard, maria follow with batcher grouping patch, jia start kernel patch PR to add remap-less path, kevin handle canary monitoring dashboards.
laura: thanks all. will post latency graphs in #eng-runtime once canary numbers come in. :thumbsup:
